reuse.why: Reuses link.findOrCreateBank, bankSync.syncAccount, handleSyncResponse and the existing provider dispatch in sync.ts, and factors the unlink field reset into clearAccountLink shared with unlinkAccount; the Fintegra downloader is written as a fresh copy instead of sharing the identical Akahu one.

duplication.why: Collapses five near-identical link* bodies into linkBankAccount/upsertLinkedAccount and the unlink reset into one function, but downloadFintegraTransactions is a line-for-line copy of downloadAkahuTransactions.

placement.why: Link rules sit in accounts/app.ts, download logic in accounts/sync.ts, server URL in server-config.ts and types under types/models, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Every change serves the four steps; consolidating all provider link functions is broader than any single step but is the seam the rules need.

maintainability.why: One linkBankAccount carries the closed-account, duplicate-link and replace-link rules for every provider, with provider variations (bank key, fileId, notified tables) passed explicitly; the loosely typed newAccount record, the `extra` override bag and the copied downloader are the weak points.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All provider link functions, including the new Fintegra one, go through linkBankAccount; unlinkAccount uses the new clearAccountLink.

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions in sync.ts copies downloadAkahuTransactions openly (only the server key and log text differ); nothing is disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankAccount gains replaceExistingLink (step 4) passed to assertBankAccountNotLinked; fileId, tables and bankKey are pre-existing provider variations made explicit rather than special-case branches; Fintegra and every other provider call the shared function.
